Espanyol de Barcelona, S.A.D. | short name = RCDE | nickname = {{Nowrap|''Periquitos'' (Parakeets)}} {{Nowrap|''Blanc-i-blaus'' (White and Blue)}} | founded = {{Start date and age|df=y|1900|10|28}} (as ''Sociedad Española de Football'') | stadium = [[RCDE Stadium]] | capacity = 40,000{{Cite web|url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/en/events|title=RCD Espanyol - Organise your event at the RCDE Stadium|website=Rcdespanyol.com|access-date=June 7, 2026}} | coordinates = | owner = Velocity Sport Limited ([[Alan Pace]] and [[JJ Watt]]) | chrtitle = President | chairman = [[Alan Pace]] | manager = [[Manolo González]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | league = {{Spanish football updater|Espanyol}} | season = {{Spanish football updater|Espanyol2}} | position = {{Spanish football updater|Espanyol3}} | website = {{URL|https://www.rcdespanyol.com/en/|rcdespanyol.com}} | pattern_la1 = _rcde2627h | pattern_b1 = _rcde2627h | pattern_ra1 = _rcde2627h | pattern_sh1 = _rcde2627h | pattern_so1 = _rcde2627hl | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = | socks1 = | pattern_la2 = _rcde2627a | pattern_b2 = _rcde2627a | pattern_ra2 = _rcde2627a | pattern_sh2 = _rcde2627a | pattern_so2 = _rcde2627al | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = | pattern_la3 = _rcde2627t | pattern_b3 = _rcde2627t | pattern_ra3 = _rcde2627t | pattern_sh3 = _rcde2627t | pattern_so3 = _rcde2627tl | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | current = 2026–27 RCD Espanyol season }} {{RCD Espanyol sections}} '''Reial Club Deportiu Espanyol de Barcelona, S.A.D.''' ({{IPA|ca|rəˈjal ˈklub dəpuɾˈtiw əspəˈɲɔl də βəɾsəˈlonə|lang}}; "Royal Spanish Sports Club of Barcelona"), commonly known as '''RCD Espanyol''', is a Spanish professional [[sports club]] based in the [[province of Barcelona]], Catalonia. The club competes in [[La Liga]], the top tier of [[Spanish football league system|Spanish football]]. Founded in 1900 in [[Barcelona]], Espanyol currently play their home games just outside the city at the [[RCDE Stadium]], which holds up to 40,000 spectators. Domestically, Espanyol has won the [[Copa del Rey]] four times, most recently in [[2006 Copa del Rey Final|2006]]. In international competitions, the club reached the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] final in [[1988 UEFA Cup final|1988]] and [[2007 UEFA Cup final|2007]]. It has a [[Derbi barceloní|long-standing local rivalry with FC Barcelona]]. ==Name== [[File:Club Espanyol de Foot-ball 1901.png|thumb|First shield of Club Español de Fútbol]] Initially known as the Sociedad Española de Football on its foundation, the name was changed to '''Club Español de Fútbol''' in 1901. In 1906, the club folded due to financial reasons and most of the players joined the [[X Sporting Club]], which came to win the [[Catalan football championship|Campionat de Catalunya]] three times in a row before disappearing in 1908 to merge with the Spanish Jiu-Jitsu Club to be effectively relaunched as the '''Club Deportivo Español''', and in 1910, they adopted their present-day colours. Espanyol is one of several Spanish football clubs granted patronage by the [[List of Spanish monarchs|Spanish crown]] and thus entitled to use ''Real'' in their names and the [[Spanish Royal Crown|royal crown]] on their badge. This right was granted to Espanyol in 1912 by [[Alfonso XIII of Spain|Alfonso XIII]] and the club subsequently became known as the '''Real Club Deportivo Español'''.{{Cite web |title=History |publisher=RCD Espanyol |access-date=27 January 2018 |url=https://twitter.com/i/events/1272855920821760001?from_editor=true}} Following the abdication of the same king in 1931 and the declaration of the [[Second Spanish Republic]], due to prohibition of royal symbols, the club adopted the more Catalan/republican friendly name, '''Club Esportiu Espanyol'''. After the [[Spanish Civil War]], the name was reverted. The club took the Catalan spelling for its name in February 1995. The word "''Deportiu''" in Reial Club Deportiu Espanyol de Barcelona is a Catalanised form of the original word "''Deportivo''" ([[Castilian language|Castilian]]), despite the correct word being "''Esportiu''" in the Catalan language. This choice was made in order to retain the initials "RCD" in the club's name. ==History== ===Foundation and club culture=== Espanyol was founded on 28 October 1900 by [[Ángel Rodríguez (footballer, born 1879)|Ángel Rodríguez Ruiz]], an engineering student at the [[University of Barcelona]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/ca/noticia/homenatge-a-angel-rodriguez/10160 |title=Homenage a Ángel Rodríguez |trans-title=Tribute to Angel Rodriguez |language=es |website=Rcdespanyol.com |date=28 October 2019 |access-date=20 April 2024 }} The club's original home was in the well-off district of [[Sarrià-Sant Gervasi|Sarrià]]; Espanyol was the first club in Spain formed exclusively by Spanish fans of the game, with the other early clubs having links to Britain or central Europe. File:RCD Espanyol campions 1904.jpg|CD Espanyol de Barcelona, Catalan champions in 1904 File:RCD Espanyol 1912.jpg|RCD Español in 1912 [[File:Ricardo Zamora Espanyol.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|[[Ricardo Zamora]] with Español]] A friend of the club founder owned a textile business and happened to have an abundance of yellow material left over from a job. In 1910, the club changed its name to the '''Club Deportivo Español''' and at the proposal of [[Eduardo Corrons]], the club's number one partner for many years, the club agreed to choose blue and white stripes as shirt colours and as the central colours of the club badge.{{Cite web |url=https://as.com/opinion/2018/02/08/blogs/1518082713_907481.html |title=Por qué el Espanyol se llamó Español |trans-title=Why Espanyol was called Spanish |language=es |website=As.com |date=8 February 2018 |access-date=20 April 2024 }} Blue and white were chosen in homage to the colours on the shield of the great Sicilian-Aragonese Admiral [[Roger de Lluria]], who sailed the Mediterranean protecting the interests of the Crown of Aragon in the [[Middle Ages]]. The club was successful from the very beginning, winning the first [[Catalan football championship|Campionat de Catalunya]] in 1903 and subsequently playing in the first [[Copa del Rey]] in [[1903 Copa del Rey|1903]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup1903.html |title=Spain - Cup 1903 |date=13 January 2000 |access-date=20 April 2024 }} In 1906, ''Club Español de Football'' had to suspend its activities due to a lack of players, since most of them were university students who enrolled to study at universities outside [[Catalonia]]. X Sporting Club took advantage of this as most of the remaining Español players joined them, which meant a big leap in quality for the club, and as a result the X won the [[Catalan football championship|Catalan championship]] three times in a row between 1905 and 1908, beating the likes of [[FC Internacional]] and [[FC Barcelona]] for the title.{{Cite web |url=https://www.cihefe.es/cuadernosdefutbol/2021/10/despejando-la-ecuacion-el-papel-del-club-x-en-la-fundacion-del-rcd-espanyol-de-barcelona-1902-1909/ |title=Nou Velòdrom de Barcelona |trans-title=Clearing the equation: the role of Club X in the founding of RCD Espanyol de Barcelona (1902 – 1909) |publisher=Chiefe |date=16 September 2021 |access-date=27 July 2022 |archive-date=23 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220523013707/https://www.cihefe.es/cuadernosdefutbol/2021/10/despejando-la-ecuacion-el-papel-del-club-x-en-la-fundacion-del-rcd-espanyol-de-barcelona-1902-1909/ |url-status=dead }} This historic side had the likes of [[Pedro Gibert (footballer)|Pedro Gibert]], [[José Irízar]], and [[Santiago Massana]]. It was not until 1909 that X and Español were restructured again, when several of the former university students returned to [[Barcelona]] with the idea of refounding ''Club Español de Football'', which they achieved on 27 December 1908, when X merged with the Spanish Jiu-Jitsu Club. In the 1910s, they won the [[Catalan football championship|Campionat de Catalunya]] three times, in 1911–12, 1914–15, and 1917–18, winning later largely thanks to their backline led by [[Ricardo Zamora]]. They also reached the final of the Copa del Rey twice in [[1911 Copa del Rey|1911]] and [[1915 Copa del Rey|1915]], but lost to [[Athletic Bilbao]] on both occasions.{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup1915.html |title=Spain - Cup 1915 |date=19 January 2000 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=28 July 2022 }} In 1994, Espanyol created its [[reserve team]], [[RCD Espanyol B|Espanyol B]],{{Cite web |title=Squad of Espanyol B 1994-95 Tercera División |url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/c/plantilla.html?temporada=693&club=Espanyol%20B |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=Bdfutbol.com}} currently playing in the [[Segunda División B]]. ===Two UEFA Cup finals (1988–2009)=== [[Javier Clemente]] was hired in 1986. In his first season, he took the team to a joint-best third place, qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. They defeated [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], [[A.C. Milan]], [[Inter Milan]], [[TJ Vitkovice]], and [[Club Brugge KV]] to reach the [[1988 UEFA Cup Final|final]], losing on penalties to [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] after a 3–3 aggregate draw.{{cite news |title=El Espanyol tocó la gloria ante el Bayer Leverkusen|trans-title=Espanyol touched glory against Bayer Leverkusen|url=https://twitter.com/i/events/1272855055834603520?from_editor=true|access-date=28 February 2020 |work=Mundo Deportivo |date=4 May 2013 |language=es}} Two relegations followed, but the club remained in La Liga from winning the [[1993–94 Segunda División]] until relegated at the conclusion of the 2019-20 COVID pandemic impacted season. Juli Pardo oversaw the transformation of the club into a [[Sociedad Anónima Deportiva]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.ccma.cat/esport3/mor-juli-pardo-ex-president-de-lespanyol/noticia/2854993/|date=11 May 2018|title=Mor Juli Pardo, expresident de l'Espanyol|language=ca|publisher=[[Corporació Catalana de Mitjans Audiovisuals]]}} In the wake of the accumulated debt, the club were forced to sell the [[Sarrià Stadium]], which was eventually demolished in 1997. [[Paco Flores]]' Espanyol won the [[2000 Copa del Rey Final]] 2–1 against [[Atlético Madrid]] at [[Mestalla]], a first cup win since 1940.{{cite news |last1=Segurola |first1=Santiago |title=El Espanyol se corona en Mestalla|trans-title=Espanyol crowned in Mestalla |url=https://twitter.com/i/events/1272855055834603520?from_editor=true |access-date=28 February 2020 |work=El País |date=28 May 2000 |language=es}} Six years later, under [[Miguel Ángel Lotina]], the club won again, this time 4–1 against [[Real Zaragoza]] in Madrid, with goals by [[Raúl Tamudo]], [[Luis García (footballer, born 1981)|Luis García]] (two) and [[Ferrán Corominas|Coro]].{{cite news |title=El Espanyol conquista su cuarta Copa del Rey |trans-title=Espanyol win their fourth Copa del Rey|url=https://z-m-www.facebook.com/events/887060308483259/ |access-date=28 February 2020 |work=El Mundo |date=12 April 2006 |language=es}} [[File:Real Club Deportivo Espanyol league performance 1929-present.svg|thumb|Chart of RCD Espanyol league performance 1929–present]] With this cup win, Espanyol entered the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]]. They won all their group games, before dispatching [[A.S. Livorno Calcio|Livorno]], [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]], [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], and [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] to reach the [[2007 UEFA Cup final|final]]. In the final, held on 16 May at [[Hampden Park]] in [[Glasgow]], Espanyol fell to fellow La Liga side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], losing 3–1 in a shootout following a 2–2 draw.{{cite web|url=https://z-m-www.facebook.com/events/887060308483259/|title=Palop ensures cup joy for Sevilla|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=17 May 2007}} They became the only football team in UEFA Cup history to remain unbeaten in the tournament, yet not take home the trophy. [[Walter Pandiani]], who would leave the club at the end of the season, was the UEFA Cup's top goalscorer that season. On 9 June 2007, Tamudo became Espanyol's highest-ever goalscorer after surpassing the 111 goals scored by [[Rafael Marañón]], and ended the night with 113. On 31 May 2009, Espanyol played its last match at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys|Estadio Olímpico de Montjuic]], a 3–0 defeat of [[Málaga CF|Málaga]]. Espanyol had played in the Estadi Olímpic after moving from their previous ground in Sarria. With the move, club talisman Raúl Tamudo had the unique distinction of having played in three different home stadiums with his club: Sarrià, Montjuïc and, beginning in the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]], the Cornellà-El Prat. ===Recent years (2009–present)=== [[File:Espanyol 24.jpg|thumb|[[Iván Alonso]] in action during a La Liga fixture in August 2009]] In January 2009, former Espanyol defender [[Mauricio Pochettino]] was hired as manager with the club in the relegation zone – his first senior job.{{cite news |title=Pochettino replaces luckless Mané at Espanyol |url=https://en-gb.facebook.com/events/986261505144523/ |access-date=28 February 2020 |publisher=UEFA |date=20 January 2009}} He won 2–1 against rivals Barcelona at the Camp Nou in February to help keep the club up; Barcelona, under [[Pep Guardiola]], won the [[Treble (association football)|treble]] that season.{{cite news |last1=Bate |first1=Adam |title=How Mauricio Pochettino's Espanyol beat Pep Guardiola's Barcelona |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/10592713/how-mauricio-pochettinos-espanyol-beat-pep-guardiola8217s-barcelona |access-date=28 February 2020 |publisher=Sky Sports |date=1 October 2016}} After 12 seasons playing at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys|Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc]], Espanyol moved to the [[RCDE Stadium|Estadi de Cornellá-El Prat]]. The new stadium was officially inaugurated on 2 August 2009 with a match between Espanyol and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]; Espanyol won 3–0, with [[Luis García (footballer, born 1981)|Luis García]] scoring the first goal at the ground, followed by a [[Ben Sahar]] double.{{cite news |last1=Collins |first1=Ben |title=Reds suffer pain in Spain |url=https://en-gb.facebook.com/events/986261505144523/ |access-date=28 February 2020 |date=2 August 2009}} Six days later, Espanyol captain [[Daniel Jarque]] died from a [[cardiac arrest]] aged 26 in the [[Florence]] neighbourhood of [[Centro Tecnico Federale di Coverciano|Coverciano]], where the club was at the time after playing several fixtures in Italy.{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8191861.stm|title=Espanyol stunned by Jarque death|publisher=BBC|date=8 August 2009}} Since then, in the 21st minute – his former shirt number – of every Espanyol match, an ovation is made in his honour for a full minute. After Pochettino left in 2012, the club maintained their position in the top flight under a series of other managers. In January 2016, Chinese businessman Chen Yansheng took over the club by acquiring a 54% stake.{{cite news |title=New Espanyol owner aiming for Champions League within three years |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jan/22/espanyol-owner-chen-yansheng-champions-league |work=The Guardian |date=22 January 2016}} In the [[2018–19 La Liga|2018–19 season]], Espanyol finished 7th, thus returning to the Europa League for the first time since their final run in 2006–07.{{cite news |last1=Gillingham |first1=Geoff |title=Friendly Europa League draw for Sevilla, Getafe and Espanyol |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/08/30/5d691c1946163f523b8b45e2.html |access-date=28 February 2020 |work=Marca |date=30 August 2019}} However, the club suffered relegation for the first time since 1994 the following season, after a 1–0 loss at Barcelona.{{cite web|first=Calum|last=Roche|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/07/08/football/1594233987_144957.html|title=Barcelona keep title race alive as they relegate rivals Espanyol|date=9 July 2020|work=Diario AS|access-date=8 July 2020|archive-date=20 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420020859/https://en.as.com/en/2020/07/08/football/1594233987_144957.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|title=Espanyol slip away to Barcelona's tune but the silence will sting too |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2020/jul/09/espanyol-slip-away-to-barcelonas-tune-but-the-silence-will-sting-too |work=The Guardian|author=Sid Lowe|date=9 July 2020}} On 3 August 2020 the club published an official statement urging La Liga to suspend relegation; nevertheless relegation was not avoided.{{citation | title=RCD Espanyol de Barcelona Comunicado Oficial | url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/es/actualidad/comunicado-oficial/_n:11399/ | date=3 August 2020}} Espanyol won promotion back to La Liga at the first attempt on 8 May 2021 following a 0–0 draw against [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]], with four matches to spare in the 42-game season. Since 2022, Espanyol have been involved in a strategic cooperation with LEYU SPORTS, who became the official Asian partner of the club.{{Cite web |title=乐鱼与西班牙人达成战略合作，共创数字体育新潮流 - IT之家 |url=https://www.ithome.com/0/638/094.htm |access-date=2022-12-02 |website=Ithome.com}} On 28 May 2023, Espanyol were relegated to the Segunda División after two seasons in La Liga. Following a 4th place finish in the Segunda División, the club was promoted back to La Liga following a promotion 2–0 (2–1 aggregate) win against Real Oviedo on 23 June 2024.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}}{{Cite web |date=2024-06-23 |title=Espanyol wins promotion playoffs to return to top tier of Spanish soccer |url=https://apnews.com/article/espanyol-oviedo-promotion-liga-1919a5ad849495dc0ad406f8678788c9 |access-date=2025-12-22 |website=AP News |language=en}} On October 8, 2025, Velocity Sports Partners (VSP) announced that it had completed the acquisition of a majority stake in the Spanish club. VSP is the sports investment arm of ALK Capital.{{Cite web|url=https://alkcapital.com/2025/10/velocity-sports-partners-complete-acquisition-of-rcd-espanyol-de-barcelona/|title=Velocity Sports Partners complete acquisition of RCD Espanyol de Barcelona|work=ALK Capital|access-date=2025-10-11|language=en}} ==Rivalries== ===''El derbi barceloní''=== {{Main article|Derbi barceloní}} In the first half of the 20th century during the [[Dictatorship of Primo de Rivera|Miguel Primo de Rivera dictatorship]] (1923–1930), FC Barcelona was seen as a symbol of [[Catalans|Catalan]] identity. This contrasted with RCD Espanyol which cultivated alignment with the central authority.{{cite web|url=http://www.iss.europa.eu/index.php?id=18&no_cache=1&L=1&tx_ttnews%5Bpointer%5D=41&tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=697&tx_ttnews%5BbackPid%5D=232&tx_ttnews%5Bpage%5D=1&cHash=2becc765c6|title=European football cultures and their integration: the 'short' Twentieth Century|date=March 2002|access-date=1 July 2009|work=Europa (web portal)|last=Missiroli|first=Antonio}} In 1918, the municipalities of Catalonia promoted a campaign to ask the Spanish Government for a [[Statute of Autonomy of Catalonia|Statute of Autonomy]]. FC Barcelona joined that request and the Catalan press recognised FC Barcelona as a major cultural arm of the Catalan independence movement. The city's other team, RCD Espanyol, dissociated itself from the claim due to the former's success on the European stage.{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.eu/article/fc-barcelona-catalonia-independence-upheaval/|title=In troubled times, FC Barcelona defines modern Catalonia|first=Jimmy|last=Burns|date=November 6, 2017|website=POLITICO}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.barcelona.de/en/fc-barcelona-barca.html|title=FC Barcelona, more than a club|website=Barcelona.de}} Today FC Barcelona is the club that is closer to the political powers in Catalonia. Its last presidents have linked the club with the [[Catalan independence|Catalan independence movement]] and the holding of a referendum, even though this causes discomfort among some Catalan fans and those in the rest of Spain who feel neglected and think the team is biased against them.{{Cite news|url=http://www.esdiario.com/864128562/El-Barca-cae-en-su-trampa-con-el-tuit-de-la-verguenza-de-Bartomeu.html|title=El Barça cae en su trampa con el tuit de la vergüenza de Bartomeu|last=Temprano|first=Alejandra|date=2016-01-11|work=[[esdiario.com]]|access-date=2017-06-17}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Although some of RCD Espanyol's directors have expressed pro-independence stances, the club stays out of politics. It is believed that most of the team's fans are against the independence of Catalonia.{{Cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/09/10/futbol/equipos/espanyol/1441906568.html|title=Joan Collet: "Vamos a dar guerra al Madrid"|date=2015-09-10|website=MARCA.com|language=es|access-date=2017-06-17}} On numerous occasions RCD Espanyol has complained of unfavourable treatment towards the club in favour of FC Barcelona by some sections of Catalonian public media such as [[TV3 (Catalonia)|TV3]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/deportes/2017/01/12/587777ec468aebd26a8b466d.html|title=El Espanyol "exige" la retirada de la campaña 'Si sientes el Barça, sientes Cataluña'|work=ELMUNDO|access-date=2017-06-17|language=es}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.elperiodico.com/es/noticias/deportes/espanyol-indignacion-texto-ensenayment-generalitat-4946067|title=Ensenyament retira un texto ofensivo con el Espanyol|author=SERGI LÓPEZ-EGEA |date=2016-03-03|work=El Periódico|access-date=2017-06-17|language=es}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.economiadigital.es/politica-y-sociedad/el-espanyol-y-el-joventut-denuncian-pensamiento-unico-en-cataluna_188315_102.html|title=El Espanyol y el Joventut denuncian pensamiento único en Cataluña|work=Economiadigital|access-date=2017-06-18}} Despite these differences in ideology, the ''derbi'' (derby) has always been more relevant to Espanyol supporters than those of Barcelona (who hold [[El Clásico]] in higher regard instead) due to the difference in objectives.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}} Though it is the most played local derby in the history of La Liga, it is also the most unbalanced, with Barcelona overwhelmingly dominant. In the league table, Espanyol has only managed to finish above Barça on three occasions in almost 70 years and the only all-Catalan Copa del Rey final was won by Barça in 1957. Espanyol has the consolation of achieving the largest margin win with a 6–0 victory in 1951. Espanyol achieved a 2–1 win against FC Barcelona during the 2008–09 season, becoming the first team to defeat Barcelona at Camp Nou in their treble-winning [[2008–09 FC Barcelona season|season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/10592713/how-mauricio-pochettinos-espanyol-beat-pep-guardiola8217s-barcelona|title=How Mauricio Pochettino's Espanyol beat Pep Guardiola's Barcelona|publisher=skysports.com|date=1 October 2016}} Espanyol lost 0–1 to FC Barcelona on 8 July 2020, to be relegated to the Segunda División. ==Stadium== {{Main article|RCDE Stadium}} From 1923 until 1997, Espanyol played their home games in [[Sarrià Stadium|Estadi de Sarrià]] in the [[Sarrià-Sant Gervasi]] district of Barcelona. In 1997, they moved to the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]] on [[Montjuïc]]. For the beginning of the 2009–10 season, Espanyol moved into the newly constructed [[RCDE Stadium]] (also known as '''Estadi Cornellà-El Prat''') between [[Cornellà de Llobregat]] and [[El Prat de Llobregat]]. File:Sarrià.jpg|[[Sarrià Stadium|Estadi de Sarrià]] File:Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc - Barcelona's 1992 Olympic Stadium.jpg|[[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys|Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc]] File:Estadicornellaelprat 3.jpg|[[RCDE Stadium]] ==Competition summary== {{Main|List of RCD Espanyol seasons|RCD Espanyol in European football}} *'''87''' ''seasons in [[La Liga|Primera División]]'' *'''6''' ''seasons in [[Segunda División]]'' *'''8''' ''participations in [[UEFA Cup]] / [[UEFA Europa League]]'' *'''2''' ''participations in [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]]'' *'''2''' ''participations in [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]]'' ===Achievements=== *In 1928, Espanyol became a founding member of [[La Liga]], and in 1929, the team won their first [[Copa del Rey]]. Espanyol has completed the highest number of seasons in La Liga without winning the title. *The team has qualified for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup/Europa League]] eight times (including the qualifications following their [[1999–2000 Copa del Rey|2000]] and [[2005–06 Copa del Rey|2006]] Spanish Cup wins, which in earlier eras would instead have granted entry to the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]]). *Espanyol reached the UEFA Cup final in [[1988 UEFA Cup Final|1988]],{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/10/22/il-milan-gia-disperato.html|title=Il Milan è già disperato|author=Licia Granello|newspaper=[[la Repubblica]]|date=October 22, 1987|page=25|language=it}}{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/11/05/un-milan-senza-attacco-una-partita-senza.html|title=Un Milan senza attacco Una partita senza storia|author=Licia
